finding: A developer whose project has the hook but no docs/spec/dependency-rules.dsl never sees the skip notice. The entry echoes the notice and exits 0, but pre-commit shows the output of a passing hook only when the hook sets verbose: true, so the commit shows only 'Passed'. The review checked this with pre-commit on a local hook that echoes the notice and exits 0: the run printed 'dc....Passed' and no notice. The tests of RL-10-IT-02 run the entry from a plain .git/hooks/pre-commit script, so they see the notice and miss the gap. The behavior looks undocumented, not intended: BR-066 and the proposal say the hook prints the notice and do not say for whom. The smallest fix needs a decision by the owner of BR-066, the domain-modeling agent. Either set verbose: true on the hook, which also prints the JSON report of dependency-check on every passing commit, or state in BR-066 that the notice shows only under pre-commit run --verbose.
why_this_severity: The hook passes without uv and without the script, which is what the scenario needs, and fitting leaves the hook out of a project without the rules file, so the case arises only when a project removes the file later (no to fails_purpose). A developer in that project sees 'Passed' and does not learn that the gate no longer runs.
